questions.stem: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-renowned exponent of which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a legendary sitar maestro who popularised Indian classical music worldwide and collaborated with The Beatles. The sitar is a plucked string instrument. His daughter Anoushka Shankar is also a sitar player; Norah Jones is his other daughter.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Ustad Zakir Hussain was a celebrated maestro of which instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Zakir Hussain was a world-famous tabla virtuoso, son of Ustad Alla Rakha. The tabla is a pair of hand drums central to Hindustani classical music. Zakir Hussain was a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan and multiple Grammy Awards.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Ustad Bismillah Khan, a Bharat Ratna awardee, was associated with which instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan was the legendary shehnai maestro who elevated the shehnai (a wind instrument) to the concert stage. He famously played at the Red Fort on India's first Independence Day (1947) and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The tabla belongs to which category of musical instruments?
questions.explanation: The tabla is a percussion instrument, specifically a membranophone (sound produced by a vibrating stretched membrane/skin). String instruments like the sitar are chordophones; wind instruments like the flute are aerophones; instruments like cymbals are idiophones.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a renowned exponent of which instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a legendary exponent of the bansuri (the Indian bamboo flute), a wind instrument. He elevated the humble bamboo flute to the level of a serious classical concert instrument and is a Padma Vibhushan awardee.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a maestro of which string instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a celebrated sarod maestro. The sarod is a fretless plucked string instrument with a deep, weighty sound, distinct from the sitar. He belongs to a long lineage of sarod players (the Bangash gharana) and is a Padma Vibhushan awardee.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma popularised which instrument in Indian classical music?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma is credited with popularising the santoor (a hammered dulcimer / trapezoid string instrument from Kashmir) as a mainstream Indian classical concert instrument. He also formed a famous duo with flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia ('Shiv-Hari') composing film music.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Mridangam' is a percussion instrument primarily associated with which classical music tradition?
questions.explanation: The Mridangam is the principal percussion instrument of Carnatic (South Indian) classical music, a barrel-shaped double-headed drum. It is the Carnatic counterpart to the tabla in Hindustani music. The ghatam (clay pot) and kanjira are other Carnatic percussion instruments.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Sarangi' is best described as which type of instrument?
questions.explanation: The sarangi is a bowed string instrument (played with a bow, like a violin) known for closely imitating the human voice, often used to accompany vocal music in Hindustani classical. This distinguishes it from plucked strings like the sitar/sarod. Pandit Ram Narayan was a famous sarangi exponent.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: M. S. Subbulakshmi, the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, was renowned as a:
questions.explanation: M. S. Subbulakshmi was a legendary Carnatic vocalist and the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna (1998). She was also the first Indian musician to perform at the UN General Assembly. Her rendition of the Vishnu Sahasranamam and Suprabhatam are iconic.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Veena' (Saraswati Veena) is traditionally associated with which goddess and music tradition?
questions.explanation: The Veena (specifically the Saraswati Veena) is a plucked string instrument traditionally associated with Goddess Saraswati (the goddess of knowledge, music, and arts) and is prominent in Carnatic classical music. It is one of the oldest Indian instruments, mentioned in ancient texts.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Ustad Alla Rakha, a legendary tabla player, was the father of which famous musician?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alla Rakha, a renowned tabla maestro who frequently accompanied Pandit Ravi Shankar, was the father of Ustad Zakir Hussain (also a tabla legend). This father-son tabla lineage is one of the most celebrated in Hindustani music.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which instrument is a wind instrument?
questions.explanation: The shehnai is a wind instrument (aerophone), traditionally played at weddings and auspicious occasions. The sarod and santoor are string instruments, and the tabla is a percussion instrument. Other Indian wind instruments include the bansuri (flute) and nadaswaram (South Indian).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Nadaswaram', a large wind instrument considered auspicious in South Indian temple music, is usually accompanied by which percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: The Nadaswaram (a large double-reed wind instrument) is traditionally accompanied by the Thavil (a barrel-shaped percussion drum) in South Indian temple and wedding music. This Nadaswaram-Thavil pairing is considered highly auspicious ('mangala vadya'). The mridangam accompanies concert Carnatic music rather than temple processions.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of these instruments is a 'ghatam', used in Carnatic music?

options.text: A clay pot used as a percussion instrument

questions.explanation: The ghatam is a clay pot (earthenware) used as a percussion instrument in Carnatic music, played by striking its surface and mouth with the hands and fingers. Despite its simple form, it produces a wide range of tones and is a respected concert instrument. T. H. Vinayakram is a famous ghatam exponent.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, a Bharat Ratna awardee, was renowned as a:
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was a towering Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008. He is also famous for the 'Mile Sur Mera Tumhara' national integration song. He was a vocalist, not an instrumentalist.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Pakhawaj' is a percussion instrument primarily used to accompany which vocal/instrumental style?
questions.explanation: The Pakhawaj is a barrel-shaped, two-headed drum traditionally used to accompany the Dhrupad style (the oldest, most austere form of Hindustani classical vocal music) and the been/rudra veena. It is considered an ancestor of the tabla. Qawwali typically uses the dholak and tabla.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which legendary musician was known as the 'Sitar maestro' and collaborated famously with The Beatles' George Harrison?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar collaborated famously with George Harrison of The Beatles, teaching him the sitar and bringing Indian classical music to Western audiences in the 1960s. While Vilayat Khan and Nikhil Banerjee were also great sitarists, Ravi Shankar is the one specifically linked with Harrison and the global popularisation of the sitar.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Dholak' and 'Dhol' are examples of which class of instruments?
questions.explanation: The Dholak and Dhol are percussion instruments (drums/membranophones), widely used in folk music, Bhangra, and celebrations across India. The dhol is larger and louder (associated with Punjab/Bhangra), while the dholak is a smaller hand drum used in folk and light classical music.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which instrument did the maestro U. Srinivas make famous in Indian classical (Carnatic) music?
questions.explanation: U. Srinivas (Mandolin Srinivas) was a prodigy who pioneered the electric mandolin in Carnatic classical music, adapting this Western instrument to Indian classical forms. Although the violin (option B) is also a Western import adopted into Carnatic music, Srinivas is specifically famous for the mandolin.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Classify the following correctly: sitar, tabla, shehnai, ghatam. Which classification is fully correct?

options.text: Sitar – string; Tabla – percussion; Shehnai – wind; Ghatam – percussion
Sitar – wind; Tabla – string; Shehnai – percussion; Ghatam – wind
Sitar – percussion; Tabla – wind; Shehnai – string; Ghatam – string

questions.explanation: Correct classification: Sitar = string (chordophone, plucked), Tabla = percussion (membranophone, drum), Shehnai = wind (aerophone, reed), Ghatam = percussion (idiophone, clay pot). This tests the four main families of instruments — a common exam format. Only option A maps each instrument to its true family.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of musician and instrument is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Option C is INCORRECT. Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was associated with the SANTOOR, not the sarod. The sarod is associated with Ustad Amjad Ali Khan (and Ustad Ali Akbar Khan). The other pairings are correct: Bismillah Khan–Shehnai, Zakir Hussain–Tabla, Hariprasad Chaurasia–Flute (bansuri).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Rudra Veena' (Been) is most closely associated with which ancient and austere style of Hindustani vocal/instrumental music?
questions.explanation: The Rudra Veena (Been) is most closely associated with the Dhrupad style, the oldest and most austere/meditative form of Hindustani classical music, accompanied by the pakhawaj. Khayal is a more ornamental later vocal form; thumri is a light romantic style; ghazal is a poetic song form.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Dr. L. Subramaniam and the late Lalgudi Jayaraman are renowned exponents of which instrument in Indian classical music?
questions.explanation: Dr. L. Subramaniam and Lalgudi Jayaraman are renowned violinists in Carnatic classical music. The violin (a Western import) was adapted into Carnatic music in the 18th–19th centuries and is now integral to it, both as accompaniment and as a solo concert instrument. The sarangi is its closest Hindustani bowed-string counterpart.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Sarod' differs from the 'Sitar' primarily in that the sarod:

options.text: Is a wind instrument while the sitar is a string instrument
Is played with a bow while the sitar is plucked
Has a fretless fingerboard (metal plate) producing a smooth glide, whereas the sitar has frets

questions.explanation: Both the sarod and sitar are plucked string instruments, but the sarod has a FRETLESS fingerboard (a smooth metal plate) that allows continuous gliding between notes (meend), producing a deep, weighty tone. The sitar has movable frets and sympathetic strings, giving a brighter, more resonant sound. Neither is bowed or a wind instrument.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which musical instrument is traditionally depicted in the hands of Goddess Saraswati and is regarded as the 'mother of all string instruments' in Indian classical tradition?

options.option_text: Sitar — plucked string prominent in Hindustani classical music
Veena — ancient plucked string revered as Saraswati's divine instrument
Santoor — struck string instrument originating from the Kashmir valley
Sarod — plucked instrument rooted in the Afghan-Indian musical heritage

questions.explanation: The Veena is the instrument held by Goddess Saraswati in traditional iconography and is called the 'mata' (mother) of string instruments in ancient Indian texts. The Sitar is a common distractor but is a relatively modern instrument (18th century), whereas the Veena dates back to Vedic times and the Natyashastra.

questions.stem: The town of Miraj in Sangli district, Maharashtra, has received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag primarily for the craftsmanship of which musical instruments?

options.option_text: Mridangam and Ghatam — clay-pot percussion instruments of South India
Tabla and Pakhawaj — traditional North Indian barrel-shaped percussion drums
Sitar and Tanpura — string instruments hand-crafted by Miraj artisans
Sarangi and Sarod — bowed and plucked strings of the North Indian style

questions.explanation: Miraj (Sangli, Maharashtra) is a celebrated instrument-making hub and holds GI tags for the Sitar and Tanpura crafted there, prized by classical musicians globally. Mridangam and Ghatam are South Indian instruments with no manufacturing lineage in Miraj. Sarod is not a GI-tagged Miraj product.

questions.stem: The 'Ghatam', a clay pot used as a percussion instrument in Carnatic classical music, belongs to which category of the Hornbostel-Sachs instrument classification system?

options.option_text: Membranophone — sound produced by a vibrating stretched animal-skin membrane
Aerophone — sound generated by a vibrating enclosed column of blown air
Idiophone — the instrument's own solid body vibrates to produce sound
Chordophone — sound produced by the vibration of stretched strings or wires

questions.explanation: The Ghatam is an idiophone: the fired clay pot itself vibrates as a whole when struck, with no membrane, string, or air column involved. Membranophones (like Tabla) use a stretched skin head. Candidates often misclassify Ghatam as a membranophone because it resembles a drum in function.

questions.stem: Which structural feature most clearly distinguishes the Rudra Veena from the Saraswati Veena in Indian classical music?

options.option_text: Rudra Veena has two gourd resonators on a bamboo tube; Saraswati has a carved wooden body
Rudra Veena has a single carved wooden resonator; Saraswati Veena uses two gourds
Rudra Veena is played with a bow; Saraswati Veena is always plucked with fingers
Rudra Veena belongs to Carnatic tradition; Saraswati Veena is played in Dhrupad

questions.explanation: The Rudra Veena (stick zither) has a long bamboo tube with two large gourd resonators (tumbas) attached beneath, and is used in Hindustani Dhrupad. The Saraswati Veena is a South Indian Carnatic instrument with a single carved wooden body topped by a dragon (yali) head. Option D fully reverses the classical traditions.

questions.stem: The 'Ektara' is the most iconic instrument of the Baul mystic singers of Bengal. Which description best matches its construction and sound-production mechanism?

options.option_text: A two-stringed lute with a hollow gourd body used in devotional folk music
A bowed spike fiddle with a coconut shell resonator and a single silk string
A plucked zither with multiple sympathetic strings laid flat on a wooden board
A single string stretched over a small drum or dried gourd as the resonator body

questions.explanation: Ektara literally means 'one string'; it consists of one string on a bamboo or reed neck mounted on a small drum or gourd resonator, plucked to produce a continuous drone accompaniment. Option A describes the Dotara (two strings, also Baul). Option B describes a spike fiddle of the Sarangi family.

questions.stem: The 'Nadaswaram' is central to South Indian temple and wedding ceremonies. Which option correctly identifies both its acoustic classification and the GI-tag district associated with its craftsmanship?

options.option_text: Membranophone family; GI tag is held by artisans from Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu
Single-reed aerophone; GI tag belongs to artisans from Madurai district, Tamil Nadu
Double-reed aerophone; GI tag is held by artisans of Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu
Chordophone family; GI tag is registered under Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu

questions.explanation: Nadaswaram is a double-reed woodwind (aerophone) — two reeds vibrate against each other when blown, unlike a clarinet (single reed). Thanjavur district artisans hold the GI tag for its craftsmanship. Option B is the strongest distractor: Nadaswaram is indeed an aerophone, but uses a double reed, not a single reed.

questions.stem: Musicologists regard the 'Pakhawaj' as the progenitor of a modern Indian percussion instrument. With which Hindustani classical form and devotional tradition is the Pakhawaj most fundamentally associated?

options.option_text: Progenitor of Tabla; primarily associated with Dhrupad and Haveli Sangeet tradition
Progenitor of Mridangam; primarily associated with Carnatic Kritis and Bhajans
Progenitor of Dholak; primarily associated with Khayal and Thumri vocal styles
Progenitor of Damaru; primarily associated with Dhrupad and Prabandha forms only

questions.explanation: The Pakhawaj (barrel drum) is considered the ancestor of the Tabla, theorised to have been created by splitting the Pakhawaj horizontally into two pieces. Pakhawaj is the principal percussion accompaniment for Dhrupad (oldest Hindustani classical vocal form) and Haveli Sangeet (Pushti Marg devotional music at Vaishnava temples). Mridangam is Carnatic and is not descended from Pakhawaj.
